shadows.purpose: Resting white elements on tinted grounds.

shadows.name: raised
shadows.purpose: Primary content cards, floating hero cards, toasts, slider thumb.

shadows.name: float
shadows.purpose: Dialogs, bottom sheets, the weeks card.

shadows.name: focus-glow
shadows.purpose: Input focus; errors swap to 0 0 0 4px rgb(217 165 160 / 0.3).

motion.name: ease-out-expo
motion.purpose: Button press/hover, sheet slide-in, landing fetus glyph growth, weeks card entry.

motion.name: float
motion.purpose: The one ambient motion: hero cards and the New reminder badge, staggered by delay.

motion.name: sheet
motion.purpose: Dialog as bottom sheet on phones.

motion.name: reduced-motion

motion.purpose: Stops float and all transitions under prefers-reduced-motion.

narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Gentle Checkup"**

A soft, Flo-inspired world built around the mother rather than the clinic. The client's palette (leaf and fern greens, beige, sage, cream on a warm milk ground) carries almost everything; one dusty rose carries the few things meant to feel tender or urgent: hearts, the baby, danger signs and soft tints. Surfaces are rounded white cards, pill buttons and circles for dates and icons, sitting on curved tinted panels with low, ink-tinted shadows. It is light only, made for daylight at home and at the health center.

This is a web app, not a mobile app. Desktop gets a real web layout (header with section links, two-column sections, a 72rem container); phone widths borrow Flo's patterns (bottom sheets, full-width pill actions, stacked cards). Nothing imitates an app store, an install prompt or a device frame. Type is Inter alone, with extra-bold titles and a friendly single-storey "a". Motion is one slow float and short expo-out transitions, all stopped by reduced motion.

It refuses the generic SaaS hero (headline, device screenshot, feature grid) and clinical realism. Sample data is shown, but always labelled "Sample".

Behind the login the same world turns into a quiet working app. Staff (health workers and admins) get a white sidebar and top bar on the milk ground; mothers get a slim top bar and a floating bottom-nav pill. Content sits in white cards with the soft shadow, the selected place is always a mint pill with a filled icon, and roles are told apart by tint (beige admin, mint health worker, blush mother), never by a new colour. The baby is shown two ways: a soft 3D picture per trimester inside the app, and the flat baby-in-womb glyph on the public landing hero.

Booking a visit is the warmest moment of the app. Services are big white tiles with the client's flat people illustrations; small places show the service as a filled icon on a pastel blob. Days and times are white cards and chips; the one she picks turns solid leaf. A visit's state is always a small tint chip from the same palette, the same on her side and the health center's.

Recording a visit is the health worker's working moment, kept as calm as the rest: vital signs in big-numbered fields with their units inside, services toggled on as pills, and unusual values met with a quiet cream "double-check" note rather than an alarm; only impossible values are errors. The mother sees the same visit as her numbers: a blush week tile per visit, milk value tiles, and two small line charts (weight, blood pressure) that always say their values in words as well as lines.

Following up a missed visit stays gentle on both sides. Staff see open items oldest first, each led by a small rose-deep "Missed N days ago" line, with one leaf action (Log follow-up) beside a mint Rebook and the log of every try kept in place. The mother is never scolded: she gets a blush "We missed you" notice with a heart and a way to ask for a new visit.

Text reminders stay out of the way until something needs a person. Admins get an SMS log: an Automatic sending card with the SMS phone's status, three tappable count tiles, a filter card and the texts as a table or cards, each with a status chip whose outline says how settled it is (dashed waiting, solid sent, filled done). Staff see one bell line per visit; the mother sees one quiet line about her reminder, and is asked to act only when the fault is her number.

Dashboards and reports are where the counts live, and they stay as quiet as the rest. Staff open on a short rose greeting, five tappable count tiles in the SMS log's style, today's appointments beside the pregnancies due within 30 days and, for admins, two cards of line-divided figures (accounts and SMS health). Reports are one page of link tabs and a filter card over either a Summary (four totals, then a card of figures per subject, a chart-green column chart and ranked service bars) or a detail tab (a table on wide screens, cards on phones). The same page prints: on paper it becomes a plain black-on-white report with the health center's letterhead and signature lines, and every chart becomes a table.
keyCharacteristics: Greens do the work; rose is a small accent; text only in ink, ink-soft, leaf or rose-deep.
Inter only, extra-bold display and section titles, tabular numerals for every date and count.
Rounded white cards (20–36px), pill buttons, icons in soft colour circles.
Curved tinted hero panels with a faint white ring for depth.
Soft, low shadows tinted with ink; one gentle float.
Web layout on desktop, Flo patterns at phone width.
Signed-in app: white sidebar or floating bottom nav, mint active pill with a filled icon, sentence-case labels.
Booking: illustrated service tiles, a sideways day strip, Morning / Afternoon time chips, and a solid leaf pick.
Visits: unit-inside vital fields, pill service toggles, a soft cream double-check before any hard error, and labelled two-line trend charts.
Follow-ups: oldest first, a rose-deep "Missed N days ago" clue, a leaf Log follow-up beside a mint Rebook, outcome and ending chips in mint or cream, and a blush heart notice for her.

SMS: dashed, solid or filled status chips, tappable count tiles with a leaf caret, a folded "Show text", every text opening "Hi, {name}!" and signed "From: Brgy. Taysan Health Center", and rose-deep only for a text that failed or is being tried again.

Dashboards and reports: count tiles with the caret glued to the last word, line-divided figure rows with bold tabular counts, rose-deep only for a count above zero that needs someone, chart-green columns and bars that always write their counts, and a black-on-white print with a letterhead and signature lines.

rules.name: The Rose Is an Accent Rule
rules.body: Rose appears only on hearts, the baby (glyph or picture), danger signs, errors, soft tints and the few things that need her or the staff's attention (a new time to answer, a missed visit and how long ago it was, a request whose date has passed, a closed day, the waiting-request and open follow-up counts, a text that failed or is being tried again). Once a follow-up is sorted it leaves rose: reached, rebooked and came-in states are mint, the rest cream. It never becomes a primary button, a section heading colour or a large flat fill beyond blush; the solid rose-deep count badge stays 24px. On dashboards and reports a count turns rose-deep only above zero, and only when it needs someone (waiting requests, open follow-ups, missed appointments, failed texts); every other count stays ink.

rules.name: The Light Colours Don't Speak Rule
rules.body: Fern, sage and rose are fills and decoration only. Text and meaningful glyphs use ink, ink-soft, leaf or rose-deep.

rules.name: The One Tint Rule
rules.body: A tinted tile holds a white icon circle whose glyph takes the tile's own deep colour: leaf on mint or beige, rose-deep on blush.

rules.name: The Danger Rule
rules.body: Danger signs and errors are rose-deep text with a filled warning icon, on white or blush. Colour never carries the message alone.

rules.name: The Role Tint Rule
rules.body: A person's role is shown by tint pairs already in the palette: Admin beige with ink, Health worker mint with leaf, Mother blush with rose-deep. Status pairs mint and leaf (Active) or cream and ink-soft (Inactive), always with a small dot and a word.

rules.name: The Said Twice Chart Rule
rules.body: Chart series colours never carry a value alone. A chart with two series names each line at its end in 13px ink-soft semibold (no separate legend), the readout repeats every value in ink bold beside a short swatch, and a "Show as table" disclosure lists them all. Chart green and chart rose stay inside charts.

rules.name: The Visit Status Rule
rules.body: A visit's status is a 28px chip from the same tints, identical for mothers and staff: Requested is a dashed leaf border with leaf text and no fill (asked, not yet real); Confirmed and Completed are mint with leaf; Rescheduled ("New time sent") and Missed are blush with rose-deep; Cancelled is cream with ink-soft. The Today week strip repeats the map on its date circles.

rules.name: The Black on White Rule
rules.body: Everything inside a printed report is black on no fill: chips, tints, chart green, rose-deep alerts and shadows all drop, and links print as plain text. A printed value is always written, never carried by colour.

rules.name: The Outline Says How Settled Rule
rules.body: A chip's edge tells how far along it is, across visits and texts alike. A dashed outline with no fill is not settled yet: a Requested visit and a Waiting text in leaf, a text "Trying again" in rose-deep. A solid 1px leaf outline with no fill is a text Sent but not yet confirmed. A fill is an outcome: Delivered mint with leaf, Failed blush with rose-deep, Not sent cream with ink-soft (and the visit fills above).

rules.name: The Extra-Bold Title Rule
rules.body: Every display, section and dialog title is weight 800 with negative tracking. Body never goes above 600 except numbers and key values (700).

rules.name: The Tabular Numbers Rule
rules.body: Every date, week count and time uses tabular lining numerals so values never jitter as they change. The tabular class goes on the numeric element itself (a date, time, week, BP, weight or count cell), never on a whole row, card or block of mixed text: tabular figures also widen hyphens and dashes, so names and sentences inside a tabular container space oddly.

rules.name: The Gentle Wrap Rule
rules.body: Headings h1–h3 balance their lines; paragraphs and list items wrap pretty. No orphaned last words.

rules.name: The Unbroken Time Rule
rules.body: A time never breaks from its AM or PM: the shared date and time formatters put a no-break space before it, and times written into copy do the same. A short date and time inside a labelled line ("Next visit: Thu, Oct 29 · 9:00 AM") is joined with no-break spaces throughout, so the line breaks after the label, never before "· 9:00 AM"; a status after it, like "(Requested)", may still wrap. The shared date formatter (`formatDate`) returns its date with no-break spaces, so every displayed date stays whole. A Filipino hyphenated word that must stay whole (makipag-ugnayan) takes a word joiner after its hyphen. Reminder lines (staff and hers) and every SMS log slot (send and retry times, "Service · date · time", the phone-status time, the limit notice's date) join every space with a no-break space, so the sentence wraps only before the slot. Her long date lines ("Wednesday, November 4 · 1:30 PM") go through `unbroken()`, which swaps every space not after a comma for a no-break space, so the line can only break after the weekday. In JSX the joiner is a string expression, `{"\u00a0·\u00a0"}`; a `\u00a0` typed as bare JSX text is not an escape and prints as six characters. A short word that leads into a date is joined to it in the dictionary (Filipino "para sa {when}" uses no-break spaces), so no single word is left alone at a line end. Report dates come from the report formatters, which join a day with no-break spaces ("Nov 5, 2026") and keep a time with its AM or PM; a date and time in one cell are joined with a no-break middle dot. The pager joins the last two words of "Page {page} of {pages}" ("Pahina {page} ng {pages}"), so a narrow phone breaks "Pahina / 1 ng 3", never before the last number. An SMS text preview is joined on screen only: its dates ("Tue, Nov 3, 10:00 AM", "Fri, Oct 30") take no-break spaces and a hyphenated word (Mag-log, Naka-schedule) takes a word joiner after its hyphen; the stored and sent text stays plain GSM-7, which has neither character. A short tag that must stay whole takes whitespace-nowrap (Walk-in, the Filipino "May appointment"), and a count tile's last word is wrapped with its caret so the caret never starts a line alone.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Label Rule
rules.body: Small labels stay in sentence case at normal tracking: sidebar group labels, table column heads, badges, form labels and bottom-nav labels. No uppercase or letter-spaced micro-labels; the week strip's weekday letters are the one exception.

rules.name: The Web, Not App Rule
rules.body: Desktop is a website, not a stretched phone. Phone-width layouts borrow Flo's patterns, but there are no app-store badges, install prompts or device frames; the product says it works in the phone's browser. Copy says so too, texts included: "Mag-log in sa website", never "app".

rules.name: The Clear Face Rule
rules.body: Floating hero cards never cover the mother's face or the belly glyph. Phones and tablets show only the weeks card; the SMS and next-visit cards appear from 1024px.

rules.name: The Shared Header Rule
rules.body: Paired cards share header height (icon circle plus title at a 48px minimum) so their lists start and run on the same lines; tile rows top-align their titles.

rules.name: The One Place Rule
rules.body: The current place in either shell is a mint pill with leaf text and a filled icon; every other item is ink-soft with a regular-weight icon and a cream hover. Nothing else marks position. The record tab bar follows the same rule without icons.

rules.name: The Wide Row Rule
rules.body: A filter card goes to a single row only when every field still has room: four fields and their button share a row from 1280px. Below that, fields sit two per row and the button takes the full width.

rules.name: The Real Steps Rule
rules.body: Step headings carry numbers only when the sequence is real: the staff booking page, where finding the mother is step one. A form reused where the mother is already known drops the numbers.

rules.name: The Mark the Exception Rule
rules.body: In a list, only the unusual state carries a badge (a hidden purok is badged, a shown one is not); the normal state stays unmarked.

rules.name: The Brand Gives Way Rule
rules.body: In the landing header the brand mark may shrink (min-w-0) and the action group may not (shrink-0), so Log in is never pushed off screen. The compact wordmark wraps to two lines (1.1 line height) from 360 to 419px instead of truncating, and truncates only below 360px. Below 400px the header tightens: 6px gaps between brand and actions (4px inside the action group), 6px side padding on Log in, a narrower EN/FIL switch (36px pill buttons with 8px padding) and an 8px gap inside the brand mark.

rules.name: The Current Tab Shows Rule
rules.body: A tab bar that scrolls sideways on phones scrolls its current tab into view when the page loads (record tabs and report tabs), so the place she is in is never off screen; the report bar also fades its ends to say there is more.

rules.name: The Zero Minimum Rule
rules.body: A grid whose children hold long no-wrap content names its phone column as `grid-cols-1` (minmax(0, 1fr)); an implicit column sizes to min-content and pushes the page sideways (the How-it-works SMS bubble was the case). `truncate` works only when every flex parent between it and the bounded box has min-w-0.

rules.name: The Ink-Tinted Shadow Rule
rules.body: All shadows use ink (31 45 39) at low alpha with negative spread. No black, no offset hard shadows.

rules.name: The One Float Rule
rules.body: The only ambient motion is a 6s, 8px float on the hero cards and the "New reminder" badge, staggered by animation delay. Reduced motion stops it, along with every transition.

rules.name: The Two Pictures Rule
rules.body: The people illustration appears only where the picture is big (service tiles, the picker thumbnails); everywhere small uses service art. Never squeeze an illustration into a chip or blow service art up into a tile.

rules.name: The Filled Pick Rule
rules.body: In a picker the one chosen day or time is solid leaf with white text and the soft shadow; open choices are white with a line border; unavailable ones fade on cream and are disabled. Navigation keeps the mint pill; choices fill with leaf.

rules.name: The Heading Travels Rule
rules.body: On paper a heading never ends a page. Mark the heading block as a print heading (unbreakable, about 6rem reserved below); Chrome ignores break-after: avoid, so never rely on it.

dos: Do import every icon from the one icon index (Phosphor, plus the Health Icons fetus glyph). The same icon always means the same thing.
Do show the baby in the app with the trimester picture (decorative, beside written weeks), keeping all three renders in the same crop window; the glyph stays on the landing hero.
Do put feature icons in soft colour circles (fill or duotone weight); use regular-weight outlines for navigation, switching to fill for the selected item.
Do label every piece of sample data "Sample" (or "Your estimate" once she has entered her own weeks).
Do keep text in ink, ink-soft, leaf or rose-deep, and check 4.5:1 on any new tint.
Do set titles at weight 800 with negative tracking, and use tabular numerals for every date and count.
Do give paired cards the same header height so their lists align.
Do use expo-out easing (cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)) for transitions and keep the reduced-motion block intact.
Do make primary actions full-width pills at phone width and keep tap targets at 44px.
Do mark the current place in a shell with a mint pill, leaf text and a filled icon.
Do keep small labels, table heads and badges in sentence case.
Do register any new custom text-size token with the class merger so it isn't dropped next to a colour class.
Do badge only the exceptional state in a list; let the normal state stay unmarked.
Do fold secondary columns and filters on narrow screens rather than shrinking them; keep phone list cards as single whole-card links.
Do build every new booking surface from the shared service tiles, service art and slot picker (plain variant inside dialogs) rather than a new date or time control.
Do show a visit's state only with the visit status chips, the same map for mothers and staff.
Do pad the page for anything fixed above the mother bottom nav (like the summary bar) so it never covers content.
Do keep the bottom-nav tab opening on its own curve (cubic-bezier(0.32, 0.72, 0, 1), 420ms) and switched off under reduced motion; every other transition stays expo-out.
Do separate impossible values (rose-deep error) from unusual ones (ink note with a filled leaf info icon, a cream notice naming the fields, kept on the second save).
Do put a measured value's unit inside its field and beside every recorded value, and set values in tabular numerals.
Do say every chart value twice: direct line-end labels, the readout and "Show as table"; chart green and chart rose stay in charts.
Do give every focusable control the solid 2px leaf outline; where a control resets the browser outline, name the solid style in its focus-visible set.
Do make the companion action beside a leaf primary on a white card soft (mint).
Do keep a filter card's single row for 1280px and up; below that, two fields per row and a full-width button.

Do keep every time joined to its AM or PM with a no-break space, keep a short date and time inside a labelled line whole so it breaks after the label, and join Filipino hyphenated words that must not break with a word joiner.
Do let an insight tile's body fill the space under its title, clamped to three lines, with the icon at the bottom.
Do number step headings only where the steps are real; a reused form that already knows the mother uses plain headings.
Do run open follow-ups oldest first and lead each with its "Missed N days ago" clue; closed ones run newest first.
Do let a chip's edge say how settled it is: dashed for not yet, a solid outline for sent, a fill for an outcome.
Do join every space in a reminder line or SMS slot with a no-break space, and join a short leading word to its date in the dictionary.
Do ask the mother to act on a failed text only when her number was the cause; otherwise reassure her the visit stands.
Do give phone grids with long no-wrap children an explicit minmax(0, 1fr) column, and min-w-0 on every flex parent of a truncated line.
Do turn a dashboard or report count rose-deep only above zero, and only when it needs someone; every other count stays ink.
Do put the tabular class on the numeric element (a date, time, week, BP, weight or count), never on a container of mixed text.
Do keep short tags whole with whitespace-nowrap (Walk-in, May appointment) and glue a trailing caret to the last word of its label.
Do wrap a printable view in the report wrapper, hide the shell and controls with the print variant, and mark each heading block as a print heading so it travels with its first rows.

Do scroll a sideways tab bar's current tab into view on phones.

Do keep the skip link first on every page and give each page's main region `id="main"`.

donts: Don't set text in fern, sage or rose; they are too light.
Don't let rose spread beyond hearts, the baby (glyph or picture), danger signs, errors and tints.
Don't place floating cards over the mother's face or the belly glyph.
Don't add app-store badges, install prompts or device frames; this is a web app.
Don't use black or hard offset shadows; shadows are low and ink-tinted.
Don't add a second ambient motion or a fake sheet drag handle.
Don't add a second typeface, a dark theme or kicker labels above titles.
Don't set uppercase or letter-spaced micro-labels; the week strip's weekday letters (and its Today label) are the only uppercase.
Don't introduce a new colour for roles or statuses; use the existing tint pairs.
Don't put the people illustrations in small places or the blob icon art in big tiles.
Don't let an unavailable day or time look pickable; fade it on cream, strike taken times, and disable it.
Don't colour an unusual-but-possible vital sign in rose or blush; rose is for errors the form will not accept.
Don't add a separate chart legend or let a series colour be the only way to read a value.
Don't put rose on a follow-up once it is sorted; reached, rebooked and came-in states are mint, the rest cream.
Don't put a white secondary pill beside the primary on a white card; it disappears into the card.
Don't let a time wrap between the number and AM or PM.
Don't type `\u00a0` as bare JSX text; put it in a string expression.
Don't let a header's actions shrink; the brand mark wraps or truncates first.
Don't rely on break-after: avoid to keep a heading with its rows; Chrome ignores it.
Don't print colour, fills or shadows inside a report, or let a printed value depend on colour.
Don't put a second colour in a one-series chart; columns and service bars are chart green, and rose stays an accent outside charts.
Don't set the tabular class on a whole row, card or table body.
Don't put a no-break space or word joiner into a stored or sent SMS; the text stays plain GSM-7.
Don't write "ina" or "inang" for mother in Filipino copy.
